title: Particle-Vortex Duality of Hydrodynamics
authors: Cenke Xu, Matthew P. A. Fisher
abstract: Equipped with the recently recognized symmetry structure of mixed states of matter and "strong-weak spontaneous symmetry breaking" (SW-SSB), we develop a quantum particle-vortex duality of emergent model-F and model-A hydrodynamics of 2d boson/rotor systems. This duality relation demonstrates that classical hydrodynamics of 2d bosons can be described in terms of the charge symmetry $U(1)_c$, but also equivalently in terms of the dual (emergent) 1-form symmetry $U(1)^{(1)}_e$, as well as $U(1)_v$ associated with the conservation of vortices. This duality provides a bridge between the hydrodynamics of matter and magnetohydrodynamics.
summary: This work establishes a particle-vortex duality for 2D boson/rotor models undergoing dissipative dynamics. By analyzing how symmetries break (SW-SSB vs. WT-SSB), the authors show that the hydrodynamics of charge density and vortices are mathematically equivalent descriptions. This provides a unified framework connecting matter wave physics to magnetohydrodynamic concepts.
main_problem: The paper develops a quantum particle-vortex duality for emergent hydrodynamics in 2D boson/rotor systems, extending known dualities from equilibrium to non-equilibrium settings.
main_result: A robust duality is established between the hydrodynamic consequences of different symmetry breaking mechanisms (SW-SSB vs. WT-SSB) associated with charge ($U(1)_c$) and vortex ($U(1)_v$) symmetries, bridging matter and magnetohydrodynamics.
method: The analysis employs the Keldysh path integral formalism to derive effective hydrodynamic equations from Lindbladian dissipative dynamics in various quantum phases.
model_or_system: The system is a 2D quantum boson/rotor model on a lattice, governed by both a Hamiltonian (quantum coherent) and Lindblad dissipative terms. The physics is analyzed across Mott insulator, Normal fluid, and Superfluid regimes.
key_observables: Charge density ($\mathbf{n}$), phase field ($\phi$), gauge fields ($\mathbf{E}, \mathbf{B}$), and the resulting hydrodynamic modes (e.g., propagating Goldstone mode).
important_parameters: Coupling constants ($u_n, u_\phi$), dissipation rates ($\Gamma$), and symmetry breaking types (SW-SSB, WT-SSB).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on working to leading order in small parameters and often assumes finite length scales ($\xi$) for perturbative expansions.
figures_summary: Tables summarize the complex relationship between symmetry structure ($U(1)_c$ vs $U(1)_e$), spontaneous symmetry breaking type, and resulting hydrodynamic modes across different phases.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the dynamics by first establishing the quantum framework (Keldysh action), then examining specific symmetry breaking scenarios (SW-SSB, WT-SSB) in different phases (Normal/Superfluid), culminating in the general statement of the particle-vortex duality.
why_interesting: The explicit connection between charge conservation symmetries ($U(1)_c$) and dual vortex symmetries ($U(1)_e$), mediated by symmetry breaking, provides a powerful theoretical tool for understanding coupled quantum field theories relevant to condensed matter systems like superconductors or superfluids.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. The dynamical phase diagram of quantum rotor model with U(1)c symmetry. Starting with the insulator phase, after U(1)c-SW-SSB (condensing ˜ϕ), the system enters the normal fluid phase with charge density diffusion; after U(1)c-ST-SSB (condensing ϕ), the system enters the superfluid phase with Goldstone mode. The same phase diagram can also be produced starting with the superfluid phase, which is the strongly symmetry phase of U(1)v. After the U(1)v-SW-SSB (condensing ˜θ), the system enters the normal fluid, and after U(1)v-ST-SSB (condensing θ), the system enters the insulator phase of rotor.
